answer: For an open network to stay honest, plume has to be checkable by others, not just asserted by the person who did the work. That is why timber matters: each contribution should be judged on the evidence it carries, not on who submitted it. And juniper matters just as much, because a record that survives beyond one round lets newcomers see what was done and lets the community hold earlier claims to account. Put together, those three make gaming the system harder than participating in it fairly.
